structure: One primary Gaussian rank-coupling law is specified. The Adelaide evidence fixes the marginal location, scale, anatomical labels and measurement operator, but not the pairing. Dependence is supplied by an explicit working assumption: transport the external study's relative ratio dispersion and use a first-order ratio approximation to obtain a separate Gaussian correlation parameter for each target cell. This generates plausible individual virtual pairs, not recovered participants or an identified joint distribution. No target outcomes or evaluator feedback were used.
parameter_provenance: The four cell means and SDs are the supplied, rounded Adelaide Table 1 values. Normal marginal shape follows the supplied description and marginal-grid construction.
Equal cell weights are specified by the task, not estimated from Adelaide sample counts. The conflicting analytic sample counts are not used.
The values 0.9534 and 0.11 are the supplied external individual nondominant/dominant ratio mean and SD. Their quotient is used only as a relative-dispersion anchor.
Transporting that anchor across instruments, populations, ages, sexes and hand labels is a modeling assumption, not a source finding.
The first-order ratio calibration and Gaussian dependence structure are author choices. Neither paper supplies the target within-cell correlations.
The reported 89% right-handed fraction is not converted into a handedness mixture: no handedness-specific joint laws or cell proportions are available.
The seed governs simulated latent ranks only. The marginal grids are retained exactly.
requested_estimands: Mean absolute difference: compute the equally weighted mean of |R-L| over all generated pairs, in kg. This is dependence-sensitive.
Percentage differing by at least 5 kg: compute 100 times the equally weighted mean of the indicator |R-L| >= 5, including equality. This is dependence-sensitive.

Mean of both hands: compute the mean of (R+L)/2. Pairing cannot change this statistic. Using the reported cell means gives an equal-cell nominal value of 33.375 kg; the actual finite-grid value follows the supplied arrays.

Average within-cell rank correlation: compute Spearman correlation separately in each cell, using average ranks for any tied hand values, then take the arithmetic mean of the four correlations. Do not substitute a pooled correlation. Under continuous ideal Gaussian margins, the cell population value is (6/pi)*asin(rho/2), not rho itself.
limitations: The absolute-difference summaries and rank correlations are not identified by the Adelaide marginal summaries. Their numerical values are conditional on the chosen dependence law.
The external ratio dispersion pools both sexes and ages 21–88 in healthy non-left-handed adults. It need not describe any particular target sex/age cell.
Rubber-ball pressure in kPa and Jamar force in kg can have different relative measurement errors. Being dimensionless does not establish transportability of a ratio distribution.
Dominant/nondominant and anatomical right/left are not interchangeable. The anchor does not impose the external ratio mean on target anatomical hands.

The ratio calibration is a first-order approximation. Exact ratio moments under untruncated Gaussian hand distributions are not well-behaved near a zero denominator; no exact normal-ratio moment claim is made.

Normal marginal tails can include physiologically implausible strengths. This generator cannot truncate or otherwise repair those tails without violating the requirement to preserve the supplied grids.

The source excludes upper-limb symptoms or arthritis. Its margins and this assumed dependence should not be treated as representative of unselected community recruitment, clinical populations, or other recruitment settings without validation.
Finite grids and seed variation cause realized correlations and difference summaries to fluctuate. Dependence-parameter uncertainty and uncertainty in rounded source moments are not estimated.
A cell with one observation or constant hand values has undefined sample rank correlation, even though a valid permutation can still be generated.
checks_actually_performed: Analytical check: assigning the ranks 0 through m-1 to the latent left ordering makes each output cell block a permutation and therefore preserves both marginal arrays.
Analytical check: the sequential row offsets produce row_id values 0 through N-1 in group order, with right-array order unchanged.
Analytical check: averaging the eight reported hand means gives the pairing-invariant nominal both-hand mean of 33.375 kg.
Analytical check: substituting the supplied moments into the calibration gives admissible positive correlations in all four cells.
No Python execution, empirical simulation, external retrieval, or comparison with evaluator targets was performed. Input-validation checks are implemented in the code but have not been executed here.

Proposed, not executed: test reproducibility, integer dtypes and per-cell permutation integrity across several grid lengths and seeds; compare large-grid rank correlations with the Gaussian-copula formula and summarize finite-seed variation in the dependence-sensitive estimands.
